inputEvidence.summary: Likely improvement. Alpha: reference has slower entry but higher exit speed and shorter combined alpha-beta time. Investigate entry-exit compromise; do not suggest raising all speeds.

Area to investigate only. Gamma: smooth speed reduction before apex and consistent acceleration after apex. No reference advantage, no anomalous deceleration. Normal braking is not evidence of wasted time.
Area to investigate only. Delta: inferred gears oscillate while raw RPM and speed remain smooth. Calculated gear unreliable. No actual shift event is established.
Likely improvement. Alpha exit: lower RPM with slow speed recovery. Engine powerband, gear, throttle and clutch are unknown. Low RPM cannot establish engine bogging or a missed shift.

Measured opportunity. Beta: repeated spatially aligned faster section examples, higher entry speed from alpha exit. The section difference overlaps exit finding: do not add separate gains. Repeat exit approach and compare combined sections.

conclusion: Neither candidate passed both coaching-quality tests. Gemma1B strict fallback rejected both final workloads. Gemma4B passed schema on one but gave directionally unjustified coaching, then failed uncertainty validation on the other. Keep bundled 1B as requested; do not claim reliable engineer reasoning or upgrade based on these results.
